evidence.quote: Dwarf beer is called gorog in Khazalid
evidence.claim: Ale is a central Dwarf cultural motif. This does not establish the recipe or strength of any DF beverage.
An attested Dwarf-run tavern uses a creature-image name. Reserve that actual name; newly composed sign images are adaptations.

evidence.quote: Most Dwarf words have several meanings.
evidence.claim: Selected component glosses depend on context. Concatenation and the English compound reading are adaptations, not a claim to complete canonical grammar.

evidence.quote: a favourite of the weaponsmith clans
evidence.claim: The official tavern example associates tavern life with Dwarf craft workers. Anvil, hammer and axe sign motifs use glossary nouns; they do not identify the actual patrons or their guild membership.

evidence.quote: Dwarf ale is by far the most famous and sought after beverage
evidence.claim: 8th-edition brewing context corroborates using ale imagery for Dwarf hospitality; it does not equate every tavern with a brewery.

Azul supplies the metal sense. Duraz means stone or slab and Bar a fortified gateway or door. Using material and architectural imagery on a tavern sign is an explicit adaptation, not a statement of construction material or fortification.

evidence.quote: Mushrooms which grow at the back of a cave
evidence.claim: Frongol retains this specific cave-mushroom meaning. Galaz denotes gold of particular ornamental value; Gronti means giant. Newly coloured or material sign images do not create a species, dish, trophy, wealth, or historical event.

Khrum supplies a war-drum image and Klinka a chisel image. Their use as symbolic signs follows the craft/creature-imagery adaptation; it does not establish the actual patrons, professional status, or service history.
Silver and bread are attested independent concepts, not invented product or wealth claims.
The glossary distinguishes a musical horn from horn material, and attests road and thunder. Selected nouns remain literal word senses inside adapted labels.
The selected moonlight sense and the printed material, shadow, work and sunrise nouns add distinct concepts. No generic machine, dawn-direction, geology or ancestry meaning is invented.

The conjunction explicitly pairs two reviewed images. Thrag means wound, Thrynaz includes laws, Tiwaz includes rest and Skaud includes song. These are not new translations for hospital, government or tavern.

High-resolution printed text confirms Zunthrum with n. Spear, money, sunset, remembering and gift are independently attested; none assigns actual stock, wealth, a historical event or a commemorated person.
